title: Nanda Is Seized by Varuna and Rescued
story:
It happened at night, at the river. Nanda, the chief of the cowherds, had gone down alone to the Yamuna to bathe while the dark hours still lay over the water. The river was still, the stars lay scattered across its surface, and there was no one else about. The village slept, and the only sound was the water closing softly around him as he stood in the shallows.

He had not been long in the water when hands closed around him. A servant of Varuna — one of the god's attendants, a creature who could not tell that this cowherd chief, standing in the dark river at the wrong hour, was not a man to be taken — seized Nanda and drew him down beneath the surface, down through the cold and the silence, to the abode of Varuna, the lord of the waters, at the bottom of the world.

On the bank, the cowherds missed him. They had all bathed there a hundred times and thought nothing of it, but now the river seemed to have swallowed one of their own. They called his name, and no one answered. They searched the dark water with their eyes, and it gave nothing back. Fear took hold of them, and they cried out the only names that seemed to matter: "Krishna! Rama!"

Krishna came at the sound. He went to the edge of the river and understood at once what had happened. He did not hesitate, and he did not wait for help. Without a word he entered the water and went down after his father, down to the court of Varuna.

Now Varuna saw who had come into his presence. And the lord of the waters did not meet the boy as one meets an intruder. He rose and honored him with offerings and with worship, the way a host honors one far greater than himself. Then he bowed, and he spoke.

"Obeisance to you," he said, "who are the supreme Self. My servant was a fool, and did not know what he was doing; he did not understand what was right. Forgive him. And you who see all things, grant your grace to me as well."

Krishna accepted the honor without anger, and Varuna returned Nanda to him. The boy brought his father back up through the water, to the bank where the cowherds stood waiting with their fear.

When they saw Nanda step out of the river, whole and unharmed, the fear let go of them all at once. They pressed around him, asking what had happened, where he had been, whether he was hurt. But Nanda climbed out into the lamplight and the familiar faces, and for a long moment he did not speak. He had seen the lord of all the waters rise and bow to the boy he had raised as his own son, and he did not know how to begin to say it.
reflection: The story turns on a strange reversal: the father is taken, and it is the son who descends to bring him back. Varuna's apology is not to Nanda but to Krishna, and the rescue is less a battle than an act of recognition — the great god honoring the boy before a word of force is spoken.
next_story_tease: And what Nanda had seen beneath the water he would soon tell to all his kinsmen.
hero_scene: Krishna leading his father Nanda up out of the dark water of the Yamuna at night, the cowherds crowding the bank with torches, while far below the lord of the waters still bows in reverence.
